column11: I say this not as a command, but to prove by the earnestness of others that your love also is genuine.

column3: Noun from γιγνώσκω ('to know'). In 2Cor.8.7 it stands in a list of excellences (faith, speech, knowledge, earnestness, love) the Corinthians are urged to abound in further.
column11: But as you excel in everything —in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in our love for you — see that you excel in this act of grace also.

column3: δοκιμάζω names the act of testing/proving -- examining something to establish its genuineness or fitness, often through practical demonstration.

column3: Verb from δόκιμος ('approved, tested'). LSJ shows senses from assaying metals/wine to 'putting to the test' persons, and a political sense of scrutinizing fitness for office. column11: Do not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, serve the Lord.

column11: For see what earnestness this godly grief has produced in you, but also what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! At every point you have proved yourselves innocent in the matter.

column3: Noun, compound of ἐπί + γνῶσις, from LSJ 'recognition', extending to 'knowledge' of a person or fact and even 'determination' of a fact judicially. column11: For see what earnestness this godly grief has produced in you, but also what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! At every point you have proved yourselves innocent in the matter.
